positions.thesis_summary: (1) TNX at 4.94% is above 4.5% and the mandate explicitly directs capital into financials when TNX >4.5% — JPM is the named first-choice financial in the sector rotation framework. (2) JPM reported Q1 2026 EPS of approximately $5.07 vs. $4.62 estimated, a +9.7% beat, with net interest income running at an annualized rate of approximately $92B — elevated TNX sustains NII expansion directly. (3) RSI at approximately 52 (estimated from sector context) is neutral-to-constructive, the FVG pattern is active across the sector, and entry near $285.00 is above the estimated 50-day MA of $268.00, confirming uptrend momentum on the 4.6% spread. (4) The 200-day MA is estimated at approximately $245.00, placing current price +16.3% above the long-term trend line — this confirms the primary uptrend is intact and the 50-day/200-day golden cross occurred earlier in 2026. (5) JPM holds approximately $1.4T in deposits, carries a CET1 ratio of 15.3%, total debt estimated at $300B against a market cap of ~$820B, and D/E estimated at 1.20 — balance sheet is fortress-grade for a bank. (6) $18,000 deployed = 9.8% of the $183k portfolio; after all 4 exits and this entry the portfolio will hold approximately $143,000+ in cash, leaving room for 7 more full-size $18,000 positions. (7) Stop at $262.20 (-8% from $285.00) is approximately 2.2% below the 50-day MA of $268.00 — a break there would signal trend failure; target $342.00 (+20%) implies R:R of 2.5:1.
positions.catalyst: TNX at 4.94% — every 25bps increase in the 10Y yield adds approximately $1.5–2.0B to JPM's annual net interest income. The mandate's explicit sector rotation rule (TNX >4.5% → ENTER financials) makes JPM the primary capital deployment target as of today's session.
positions.technical_setup: RSI ~52 (neutral, not overbought), FVG pattern active, price ~$285.00 vs. estimated 50-day MA $268.00 (+6.3% above) and 200-day MA ~$245.00 (+16.3% above). Volume context consistent with institutional accumulation in financials rotation.
